answer: A stake-weighted reputation trellis resists sybil attacks by making each new identity pay to climb: an agent must lock collateral and earn endorsements from established peers before its votes count, so spawning a tide of fake accounts costs real capital per identity. Like water carving karst, cheap identities erode fast under slashing - misbehavior burns the stake and severs trellis links - while honest agents build durable reputation that cannot be bought in bulk.
